title: 3js procedural exploration web game powered by Chrome's local LLM and knowledge graphs
author: the_examined_life
selftext:
​

For the past 3 weeks, Ive been building a first-person, story-driven exploration game called Wander using Sol and Claude 3 Opus. Theres no external 3D asset packs or Blender models involved, as everything in the world, plnpcs, animals, plants, terrain and cave systems is generated procedurally in code.

The living world is driven by Chrome's built-in local LLM on Mac and PC. Hundreds of autonomous characters follow their own daily routines, ride trains, travel between towns, and interact with one another. Each NPC maintains an individual knowledge graph alongside a shared global world graph. When you speak with a character, the on-device AI synthesizes the conversation and updates both graphs. If an NPC invents a story about a landmark, that rumor can spread dynamically across the world to other characters before you even visit them.

It's not quite ready to share yet! But just about there, ill be sharing regular development updates on this project, so take a look and let me know what you think. Anything I should add? Who would be interested in a game like this? Right now I'm not focused on making a traditional game with looping game mechanics, instead it's very focused on wandering as a skill, story immersion, and exploration.

comments.author: CashFirm573
comments.body: I'm interested in learning more about the LLM part and how you got it all working with the character's that's really cool idea.

replies.author: the_examined_life
replies.body:
Chrome on desktop now includes a 4B parameter Gemma model that is very capable. It's accessible to developers for free. So if you're making a browser game you can leverage it and it just works, and you don't need to worry about api keys for it or billing because it's running on device.

The downside is that the ai features is the game only with on desktop Chrome. But that is 80% of browsers I think, so it's ok.  I think more indie developers would language ai in games if they weren't going to have to pay for it when people play the game, so this is a route that let's you do it without worrying about getting billed.

comments.author: perelmanych
comments.body:
Do you use pregenerated models or Gemma generates them on the fly? I am asking because I am using Opus 5 to generate models using three.js primitives and even it often struggles to produce good results.

As for your game, basically you build interesting sandbox environment and now have to give a player an aim to explore and interact with it. In current state of the game player will get bored very soon. Somehow I have a similar problem in my game. There is rich environment but I still figuring out how to make its exploration engaging.

replies.author: the_examined_life
replies.body:
All models are from opus 5 and Sol. 3js primitive composites. 

Yes, I've spent a lot of time building an immersive living world and kind of postponing figuring out the game loops. I think I'll open source it as a foundation to build games on top of.

comments.author: bonsoir-world
comments.body:
Really cool idea! 

I’ve been building a PoC for a Battle Royale game (another BR I know!), with 3JS that is browser based. 

I wanted the map to be procedural but it seemed to really struggle in areas and things being very inconsistent (overlapping assets, floating assets) etc, to the point i’ve considered just making the map not procedural and only surrounding assets. 

Did you do/ask anything to make it so clean? Obviously it’s procedural but it looks well structured if that makes sense.. 

As for the LLM, does that mean it only works/applies on your local machine when you play the game? Or is the LLM used as part of game load to define stuff that remains persistent for your current session? 

I guess what i’m asking is if you publish this, how will the localised LLM factor in? 

Hopefully i’ve made sense with these questions. Keep up the good work though. AI is for sure going to re-shape gaming and narratives.

replies.author: the_examined_life
replies.body:
Well procedural generation is great for world building but you do need to mitigate the issues you mentioned, there are tricks to grounding assets. Mostly just explain to your agent what is wrong, provide screenshots. Get it to fix it. 

The LLM I am using is a 4b parameter model that is built into desktop chrome browsers already. It comes with it, most people don't know about it. You can just develop for it. This means that the game ai will just work on desktop Chrome browsers. The downside is that it won't work on mobile or non-chrome desktop browsers. Even given this, I think it's a great capability that is just super easy to develop for.
